title: Fermentation temperature
what: The temperature the tank cooling holds during alcoholic fermentation: 14, 16 or 18 °C or cellar ambient for whites; 22, 26 or 30 °C or uncontrolled for reds.

steps: Fermenting sugar releases heat, about 1.3 °C per °Brix without cooling
a big, uncooled red tank can climb past 32 °C
yeast die and the fermentation can stick with sugar left

choose: Whites: 14–16 °C for fresh, fruity styles such as young Riesling. Reds: 26–30 °C extracts colour and tannin for structure; 22 °C gives a lighter, fruit-led red.
exam: Expect 'explain how fermentation temperature differs for white and red wines'. Contrast the aims, aroma kept against colour and tannin extracted, and end with the style.

check.question: A Napa Cabernet Lot of 25 °Brix starts fermenting at 20 °C with the cooling switched off. What is the main risk?
options: The tank overheats past 32 °C and the fermentation sticks
Nothing harmful: the heat just extracts deeper colour and tannin
The warmth speeds the yeast so it ferments dry in two days
Malolactic conversion starts mid-ferment and adds butter
check.answer: The tank overheats past 32 °C and the fermentation sticks
check.why: Without cooling, fermenting 25 °Brix could add over 30 °C; above about 32 °C yeast die fast, and the fermentation can stop with sugar left.
